intro: MIDI to MP3 turns MIDI files (.mid, .midi or .kar) into MP3 audio that plays on any phone, computer, car or speaker. A MIDI file holds no recorded sound, only the notes each instrument should play; to hear it you need a synthesiser, and here we do it for you with a bank of real instrument sounds.

We use FluidSynth, the reference free synthesiser, with the FluidR3_GM bank: the 128 General MIDI instruments (pianos, strings, brass, guitars, synths…) and drums, recorded from real instruments. Tempo and its changes, each channel's instruments, volume, panning and pedals are honoured, with reverb.

You choose the MP3 quality: 128, 192 or 320 kbps, or variable. Before synthesising we work out how long the MIDI lasts, and your plan's minute limit is the same as for the other audio tools, so a tiny file with endless notes cannot tie up the server.

It is useful for listening to a karaoke backing track, sharing a composition made in a sequencer, preparing rehearsal accompaniment or turning a collection of old MIDI files into audio. You can convert up to 20 files at once.
steps: Upload one or more MIDI files.
Download the MP3 or the ZIP with all of them.

faq.q: Why does it sound different from my keyboard?
faq.a: Every synthesiser has its own sounds. MIDI only says which note each instrument plays; here we use the FluidR3_GM bank, of high quality and with a free licence.
No: a MIDI holds no recorded voice. The lyrics in .kar files are text and are not sung.

faq.q: Can I get the sheet music?
faq.a: Yes, with MIDI to PDF, which transcribes the notes onto staves.
